Counterfeit Joint OP

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
A joint operation between the CIPC, SAPS, SARS and other brand protectors to combat the sale of counterfeit goods.

Summary:
We're in the age of immediacy fuelled by an addicition to social media. People know what everyone is wearing, what they sleep on and in, what and where they are eating and what they are driving to get there. The pressure is on and fueled by a desperation to keep up with the jonses in these tough economic times - some consumers are willing to pay the least for cheap knock-offs.

The counterfeit goods market has been labelled as the world’s fastest growing and most profitable industry and it’s reaching epidemic proportions. It's estimated to be between 7% and 10% of the world’s total trade. Due to it shipping routes, South Africa is one of the biggest markets on the continent as landlocked countries abuse it to move their counterfeit consignments. Research on the value of losses runs into the billions but is difficult to quantify because one cannot conclude that a counterfeit goods buyer would necessarily purchase the original.


Further information:
On the morning of the 22nd at 08h00 a.m approximately 40-50 SAPS officers will gather at the Provincial Operational Command Center to receive instructions on the operation taking place at a building in the CBD. Private security such as Fidelity will also be taking part as a force multiplier.

The operation commander and head of the anti counterfeit SAPS unit Brigadier Kobus Lategan will be fitted with a Go Pro cam and a mic in order to capture the action from his perspective. Instead of relying solely on engagement with the Presenter the Brig's communications to his team will help us tell the story.

We'll also fit the Presenter with a Go Pro (checking in with crew if there are two available). This way the Presenter literally walks the viewer through the raid and it's not limited to pre-written links or moments highlighted by the producer. The building location is classified until the morning of the operation.

During these ops, naturally the officers spread out and depending on the accuracy of the police information, action will be taking place in different rooms at the same time. We need to capture as much of the action as possible - the brands, the seizures, the attempted escapes, the arrests and so forth. Brigadier Lategan says in the past they have discovered “manufacturing plants” within these buildings as well as Malawians locked up for cheap labour. He's not certain if they'll find the same in this building.

We understand the building was bought for cash by a syndicate of undocumented foreign nationals who have been operating in the CBD for over 10 years. In recent years they have witnessed a surge in counterfeit products due to escalating demand for popular brands like Nike, Puma, Adidas, and other high-end items like, Louis Vuitton, Hermes, Rolex, Gucci,etc. The illicit importation through both land- and sea borders poses the most significant threat.

The SAPS is yet to disclose the nationalities at work within the building however, they have advised us the primary culprits are often Somali, Ethiopian,Senegalese,Bangladesh and Nigerian citizens.

Many of these shop owners operate within extensive family networks or large groups, distributing their merchandise widely. Typically, a single owner oversees multiple shops and purchases goods in bulk from importers to secure competitive prices. In many instances, as much as 80% of the workforce comprises illegal immigrants in the country.

These businesses predominantly hire undocumented workers such as Zimbabweans and, notably, Malawians for their affordability in labour costs. They collaborate closely with significant syndicates, exacerbating challenges further as corruption within the security sector remains a substantial issue.

Follow up in-person meeting to finalize details with Brig Lategan and Amanda on Wednesday 17th July.

Summary: We're in the age of immediacy fuelled by an addicition to social media. People know what everyone is wearing, what they sleep on and in, what and where they are eating and what they are driving to get there. The pressure is on and fueled by a desperation to keep up with the jonses in these tough economic times - some consumers are willing to pay the least for cheap knock-offs. The counterfeit goods market has been labelled as the world’s fastest growing and most profitable industry and it’s reaching epidemic proportions. It's estimated to be between 7% and 10% of the world’s total trade. Due to it shipping routes, South Africa is one of the biggest markets on the continent as landlocked countries abuse it to move their counterfeit consignments. Research on the value of losses runs into the billions but is difficult to quantify because one cannot conclude that a counterfeit goods buyer would necessarily purchase the original. Further information: On the morning of the 22nd at 08h00 a.m approximately 40-50 SAPS officers will gather at the Provincial Operational Command Center to receive instructions on the operation taking place at a building in the CBD. Private security such as Fidelity will also be taking part as a force multiplier. The operation commander and head of the anti counterfeit SAPS unit Brigadier Kobus Lategan will be fitted with a Go Pro cam and a mic in order to capture the action from his perspective. Instead of relying solely on engagement with the Presenter the Brig's communications to his team will help us tell the story. We'll also fit the Presenter with a Go Pro (checking in with crew if there are two available). This way the Presenter literally walks the viewer through the raid and it's not limited to pre-written links or moments highlighted by the producer. The building location is classified until the morning of the operation. During these ops, naturally the officers spread out and depending on the accuracy of the police information, action will be taking place in different rooms at the same time. We need to capture as much of the action as possible - the brands, the seizures, the attempted escapes, the arrests and so forth. Brigadier Lategan says in the past they have discovered “manufacturing plants” within these buildings as well as Malawians locked up for cheap labour. He's not certain if they'll find the same in this building. We understand the building was bought for cash by a syndicate of undocumented foreign nationals who have been operating in the CBD for over 10 years. In recent years they have witnessed a surge in counterfeit products due to escalating demand for popular brands like Nike, Puma, Adidas, and other high-end items like, Louis Vuitton, Hermes, Rolex, Gucci,etc. The illicit importation through both land- and sea borders poses the most significant threat. The SAPS is yet to disclose the nationalities at work within the building however, they have advised us the primary culprits are often Somali, Ethiopian,Senegalese,Bangladesh and Nigerian citizens. Many of these shop owners operate within extensive family networks or large groups, distributing their merchandise widely. Typically, a single owner oversees multiple shops and purchases goods in bulk from importers to secure competitive prices. In many instances, as much as 80% of the workforce comprises illegal immigrants in the country. These businesses predominantly hire undocumented workers such as Zimbabweans and, notably, Malawians for their affordability in labour costs. They collaborate closely with significant syndicates, exacerbating challenges further as corruption within the security sector remains a substantial issue. Follow up in-person meeting to finalize details with Brig Lategan and Amanda on Wednesday 17th July. metadata.Unique Selling Point: A joint operation between the CIPC, SAPS, SARS and other brand protectors to combat the sale of counterfeit goods.
metadata.Summary: We're in the age of immediacy fuelled by an addicition to social media. People know what everyone is wearing, what they sleep on and in, what and where they are eating and what they are driving to get there. The pressure is on and fueled by a desperation to keep up with the jonses in these tough economic times - some consumers are willing to pay the least for cheap knock-offs. The counterfeit goods market has been labelled as the world’s fastest growing and most profitable industry and it’s reaching epidemic proportions. It's estimated to be between 7% and 10% of the world’s total trade. Due to it shipping routes, South Africa is one of the biggest markets on the continent as landlocked countries abuse it to move their counterfeit consignments. Research on the value of losses runs into the billions but is difficult to quantify because one cannot conclude that a counterfeit goods buyer would necessarily purchase the original.
metadata.Further information: On the morning of the 22nd at 08h00 a.m approximately 40-50 SAPS officers will gather at the Provincial Operational Command Center to receive instructions on the operation taking place at a building in the CBD. Private security such as Fidelity will also be taking part as a force multiplier. The operation commander and head of the anti counterfeit SAPS unit Brigadier Kobus Lategan will be fitted with a Go Pro cam and a mic in order to capture the action from his perspective. Instead of relying solely on engagement with the Presenter the Brig's communications to his team will help us tell the story. We'll also fit the Presenter with a Go Pro (checking in with crew if there are two available). This way the Presenter literally walks the viewer through the raid and it's not limited to pre-written links or moments highlighted by the producer. The building location is classified until the morning of the operation. During these ops, naturally the officers spread out and depending on the accuracy of the police information, action will be taking place in different rooms at the same time. We need to capture as much of the action as possible - the brands, the seizures, the attempted escapes, the arrests and so forth. Brigadier Lategan says in the past they have discovered “manufacturing plants” within these buildings as well as Malawians locked up for cheap labour. He's not certain if they'll find the same in this building. We understand the building was bought for cash by a syndicate of undocumented foreign nationals who have been operating in the CBD for over 10 years. In recent years they have witnessed a surge in counterfeit products due to escalating demand for popular brands like Nike, Puma, Adidas, and other high-end items like, Louis Vuitton, Hermes, Rolex, Gucci,etc. The illicit importation through both land- and sea borders poses the most significant threat. The SAPS is yet to disclose the nationalities at work within the building however, they have advised us the primary culprits are often Somali, Ethiopian,Senegalese,Bangladesh and Nigerian citizens. Many of these shop owners operate within extensive family networks or large groups, distributing their merchandise widely. Typically, a single owner oversees multiple shops and purchases goods in bulk from importers to secure competitive prices. In many instances, as much as 80% of the workforce comprises illegal immigrants in the country. These businesses predominantly hire undocumented workers such as Zimbabweans and, notably, Malawians for their affordability in labour costs. They collaborate closely with significant syndicates, exacerbating challenges further as corruption within the security sector remains a substantial issue. Follow up in-person meeting to finalize details with Brig Lategan and Amanda on Wednesday 17th July.
